g.text: ↑ acceleration of the mass / acceleration of the ground
β = natural period of the building / period of the shaking →

svg.text: Shaken at its own period (β = 1), an oscillator with 5% damping moves ten times as much as the ground (1/2ζ); much stiffer (β ≪ 1) it just follows the ground; much softer (β ≫ 1)
it stays still while the ground moves under it (base isolation). A real earthquake is not a steady sine but a few seconds of broadband noise, so the measured SA/PGA peaks near 2–2.5,
not 10: there is no time to build up resonance. Damping matters most exactly at resonance.
